sources_quoted.quote: m(R) = 100 / (100 + R)   (apply_resistance, resistance.py) ... post = raw · m(R)

extracted.note: resistance mitigation is linear in raw damage for fixed R, so post-mitigation damage may be split into a magic part and a non-magic part and amplified componentwise without error (Section 1.2, mitigation linearity)

independent_computation.model: Target of the coupled roster is simultaneously Cursed (Abyssal Mask, S1) and Vulnerable (Imperial Mandate, S2). By S3 the two percent amplifiers compose multiplicatively; by S1 the curse multiplies only the magic component. Writing the participant's post-mitigation, pre-amplifier incoming damage as P (non-magic) + M (magic):
steps: The reported old value carries the Vulnerable amp but no curse term: 3022.0 = 1.07 * (P + M)  =>  P + M = 3022.0 / 1.07 = 2824.29907 (pre-amplifier post-mitigation incoming).

One clean multiplicative curse application on the magic sub-component contributes 1.07 * 0.12 * M = 0.1284 * M. Solving 0.1284 * M = 50.30 gives M = 391.744 and hence P = 2824.299 - 391.744 = 2432.555 (both non-negative; magic share 13.87% of incoming, a legal split).
Forward check under the wiki identity: 1.07 * 2432.555 + 1.1984 * 391.744 = 2602.833 + 469.467 = 3072.2999 -> 3072.3, reproducing the new value exactly at golden rounding.

The old value 3022.0 = 1.07 * (P + M) applies the Vulnerable amp to everything and applies the Unmake curse to nothing - it contains no 12% magic term at all, contradicting S1 for a target the scenario places inside the curse.

Direction check: the delta is +1.6645%, i.e. exactly the size of one 12% curse on a ~390-420 magic packet. It cannot be an amp-ordering (multiplicative-vs-additive) difference: mult minus add equals 0.07*0.12*M = 0.0084*M, and matching 50.30 would need M = 5988 > the entire incoming total, which is impossible. Nor can it be a whole-target amp change (a missing 7% would be +211.5, a missing 12% would be +362.9). The only composition consistent with the observed delta is the addition of one 12% magic-only curse application on a magic sub-component of the incoming stream - which is exactly what S1's 'from all sources' clause requires a roster scenario to pin.

Cross-check against the additive alternative: with the same M, additive stacking would give 1.07*2432.555 + 1.19*391.744 = 3069.0, not 3072.3. The published value matches the multiplicative composition mandated by S3.

frozen_baseline_analysis.reading: Under the same identity, 3269.6 = 1.07*P + 1.1984*M requires M = 1928.35 of the same 2824.30 pre-amp total, i.e. a 68.3% magic share. That is a self-consistent arithmetic solution but a different scenario decomposition, not a different formula: no single (P, M) pair reproduces any two of {3022.0, 3072.3, 3269.6} together with the third under any combination of amp scope (none / all / magic-only) and composition (multiplicative / additive) - an exhaustive 13-variant solve found zero consistent triples.
frozen_baseline_analysis.conclusion: The baseline value cannot be reconciled with either candidate under one damage split, so it reflects pre-C3 engine state that was never re-captured. It is stale, not corroborating evidence.

limits_of_this_oracle: The scenario definition (roster composition, levels, builds, fight window) lives outside the permitted evidence tree (scripts/ and tests/ were not read), so the pre-amplifier split P = 2432.55 / M = 391.74 is inferred from the leaf delta rather than recomputed from champion and item stats.

Consequently this oracle verifies the amplifier composition on the changed quantity, not the full simulation. A residual alternative that the arithmetic alone cannot exclude is a double application of the 12% curse on a ~374-unit magic packet (0.1344 * M = 50.30). It is rejected on the textual ground that S1 scopes the curse to magic damage 'from all sources' - the exact clause a roster-wide golden scenario exists to pin - and on the ground that the old value contains no curse term whatsoever, which S1 forbids for a cursed target.
